"''Someplace drier, sure. Besides, nothing ever happens on Bestine.|Two shoretroopers on Bestine IV, moments before their deaths|}} '''Bestine IV''' was a [[Waterworld|water-covered]] [[planet]] located in the [[Inner Rim Territories]]' [[Bestine system]]. One of the key members of the [[Galactic Republic]] by the [[time]] of the [[High Republic Era]], it served primarily as an [[Agriworld|agricultural world]], hosting [[starship]] manufacturing facilities as well. Bestine was also part of a [[lommite]] [[ore]] [[Hyperspace route|shipping route]] that connected the planet [[Eriadu]] to the [[Core Worlds]]. During the [[Separatist Crisis|rise]] of the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems|Separatist Alliance]], the Separatist [[Head of State|leader]] [[Count of Serenno|Count]] [[Dooku]] expressed threats to the security of the lommite shipping route via Bestine to Eriadu's [[Governor of Eriadu|governor]], [[Wilhuff Tarkin]]. Bestine IV remained loyal to the Republic during the [[Clone Wars]] against the Separatists, hosting a [[Republic Navy]] [[fleet]]. After the war [[Mission to Mustafar|ended]] with the Separatists' defeat, the Republic [[Proclamation of the New Order|became]] the [[Galactic Empire]] and brutally annexed Bestine. The new government built a [[Imperial naval base|naval shipyard]] on the local island of [[Jahnae]] to help quell potential rebellions in the Inner Rim. The new base was unpopular with the locals and forced many, including the [[merchant]] [[Jek Tono Porkins|Jek Porkins]], to leave. During the [[Galactic Civil War]], in [[3 ABY]], the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic|Rebel Alliance's]] [[Twenty-First]] [[Mission to Bestine IV (Twenty-First)|traveled]] to Bestine as part of a coordinated rebel effort. In Bestine IV's [[Bsellis City]], [[Sergeant]] [[Mey Kilrow]] of the local [[Bestine Security Force]] kept a protection deal with the planet's most ruthless gang, the [[Nova Razors]]. A warrior visited the [[Bsellis City market district|neighborhood]] where the gang operated and [[Attack on the Nova Razors|attacked]] its [[Blue Garden Homes|headquarters]], defeating the [[Unidentified Twi'lek gang leader|gang leader]] and many of his thugs. Learning of Kilrow's corruption, the warrior then sought to end it. Between 3 [['ABY-BBY' dating system|ABY]] and [[4 ABY]], the criminal syndicate [[Crimson Dawn]] [[Mission to Bestine IV|hired]] a [[T'onga's crew|crew]] of [[bounty hunter]]s led by [[T'onga]] to help [[Bestine IV insurgents|insurgents]] on Bestine IV stop an Imperial [[Unidentified Imperial transport|munitions shipment]]. The Empire learned of the syndicate's plan, and a [[Vader's crew|team]] led by the [[cyborg]] [[mercenary]] [[Beilert Valance]] was sent to set a trap for the attackers. The trap was sprung during the attack, and Valance and T'onga, two old allies, found themselves in a confrontation. There, T'onga revealed to Valance that the people the latter was working with the Empire to protect had already been taken or [[Death|killed]]. Angered about being lied to by the Empire, Valance killed the Imperial shipment's [[Coastal defender stormtrooper|shoretrooper]] security force and had the [[transport]] fly into the base on Jahnae, destroying it. Valance used the base's destruction as bait for the [[Dark Lord of the Sith|Sith Lord]] [[Anakin Skywalker|Darth Vader]], who arrived on the planet to confront the mercenary. The two fought, with Vader ultimately defeating Valance, and [[TIE/sa tactical bomber|TIE/sa bombers]] [[bomb]]ed the [[Unidentified village (Bestine IV)|village]] on Jahnae. Imperial [[Lieutenant]] [[Jyala Haydenn]] then shot the mercenary, sending him dropping off a cliff. T'onga and her crew then found Valance alive and took him offworld. ==Description== {{Quote|Not much on that planet besides a lot of water—but there is a major Imperial naval base on ''Jahnae''. It's rumored to be a top-secret R&D facility making lots of nasty weapons of ''war''—which is probably why they've driven most of the denizens offworld.|T'onga briefs her crew on Bestine IV|}} [[File:Bestine-BountyHunters29.png|thumb|left|300px|Bestine IV's surface was covered with water and featured islands.]] Bestine IV, also known simply as Bestine, was a terrestrial [[planet]] in the fourth [[orbit]]al position of the [[Inner Rim Territories]]' [[Bestine system]], near the [[Kestic Station]] [[Merchant|trading]] outpost.{{BuildXWingCite|20|Starfighter Aces}} Situated in grid square M-14 of the [[Standard Galactic Grid]], the world lay along the [[Corellian Trade Spine]] between the astronomical object [[Foless]] and the world [[Mechis III]].[[Revelations (2022) 1|''Revelations'' (2022) 1]] Appearing [[Color|blue]] and brown-green from [[Realspace|space]], Bestine was a [[Waterworld|water-covered]] world that hosted a number of islands. It possessed [[Farm|agricultural]] capabilities, with its terrain including [[Mountain|hills]], cliffs, [[cave]]s, flat plains, and [[island spires]]. It had a type I [[atmosphere]], breathable to [[human]]s and other [[species]], and its weather included thunderstorms. ==History== ===Loyal to the Republic=== ====Garnering importance==== {{Quote|Forty-two individual islands, each representing a key member of the Republic. Here visitors will be able to experience everything that the Republic has to offer, from the golden beaches of Spira and island spires of Bestine, to the bustling markets of Jaresh and fashion emporiums of Alderaan.|[[Coordinator]] [[Samera Ra-oon]], on Valo|}} [[File:Tarkin-SWE.png|thumb|right|200px|Wilhuff Tarkin helped ensure security for space around Bestine IV.]] By the [[time]] of the [[High Republic Era]], Bestine IV was considered a key member world of the [[Galactic Republic]]. At the [[Valo Republic Fair|Republic Fair]] on the planet [[Valo]] in [[231 BBY]],''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]'' those members were represented respectively by [[World Pavilions]], with Bestine's island spires being shown as a symbol of what the Republic had to offer. The [[Republic Fair|fair]] fell under [[Valo Atrocity|attack]] by the [[Nihil]] [[pirate]] marauders, who destroyed the World Pavilions. Under the Republic, Bestine IV was primarily an [[Agriworld|agricultural world]] but also hosted [[starship]] building facilities. In addition, it was part of a shipping route that saw [[lommite]] [[ore]] flow from{{HelmetCollectionCite|5|Databank A-Z}} the planet [[Eriadu]] to the [[Core Worlds]] via the planet{{Databank|fondor|Fondor}} [[Fondor]], circling around Bestine along the way,[[Tarkin (novel)|''Tarkin'']] which strengthened the world's importance. An alliance of pirate gangs in the [[Seswenna sector]], headed by [[Q'anah (pirate)|Q'anah]] of [[Q'anah's Marauders]], began [[Greater Seswenna raids|raiding]] convoys of lommite shipments that used the shipping route until they were crushed in [[46 BBY]][[Tarkin (novel)|''Tarkin'']] establishes that [[Wilhuff Tarkin]] was eighteen [[Standard year|years]] old when [[Q'anah (pirate)|Q'anah]] [[Death|died]] and fifty years old at the time of the novel's events, dated to [[14 BBY]] by ''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]''. Q'anah's death can therefore be placed in [[46 BBY]]. by the [[Outland Regions Security Force]] due to the efforts of [[Lieutenant]] [[Wilhuff Tarkin]]. Q'anah's defeat and subsequent [[Death|execution]] ensured the safety of space around Bestine IV. ====Allegiances tested==== {{Quote|I realize that you have been successful in shipping lommite through Malastare, and circling around Bestine to reach Fondor and the Core. But where will Eriadu be when Fondor opts to join the Confederacy?|Dooku questions Wilhuff Tarkin on his plans for the upcoming Clone Wars|}} After the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems|Separatist Alliance]] was founded following the [[Raxus Address]] in [[24 BBY]],''[[Rise of the Separatists]]'' states that the [[Raxus Address]] took place two [[Standard year|years]] before the [[First Battle of Geonosis]], which ''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]'' dates to [[22 BBY]]. Therefore, the Raxus Address must have occurred in [[24 BBY]]. Eriadu, which had become a major trading center in the [[Standard year|years]] after the [[Battle of Naboo|Naboo Crisis]] of [[32 BBY]], was put under pressure to join the new faction as nearby [[sector]]s [[Separatist Crisis|seceded]] from the Republic over time. In a final attempt to recruit Tarkin, who had become Eriadu's [[Governor of Eriadu|governor]], Separatist [[Head of State]] [[Count of Serenno|Count]] [[Dooku]] revealed his understanding of the significance of the shipping route via Bestine by warning that the route would soon be sabotaged by the secession of its critical planets, such as Fondor, from the Republic. [[File:Bel_Niner.png|thumb|left|305px|Clone troopers Bel and Niner were ordered to contact the Republic fleet at Bestine IV for reinforcements.]] Just [[Standard week|weeks]] later, in [[22 BBY]], the [[Clone Wars]] [[First Battle of Geonosis|began]] between the Republic and the Separatists. Eriadu and Bestine remained loyal to the Republic, and a [[fleet]] of the [[Republic Navy]] was based at the latter world. In [[21 BBY]], while [[Mission to Grievous's castle|hunting]] the Separatist [[General]] [[Grievous]] at his [[Grievous's fortress|fortress]] on the [[moon]] [[Vassek 3]]''[[Star Wars: The Visual Encyclopedia]]'' with the [[Jedi]] [[Kit Fisto]] and [[Nahdar Vebb]], [[Clone Commander]] [[Fil]] ordered the [[clone trooper]]s [[Bel]] and [[Niner]], who were guarding their [[Fil's Squad|squad's]] [[Nu-class attack/transport shuttle|shuttle]] outside the [[fortress]], to inform the fleet at Bestine IV that they had engaged Grievous and required reinforcements. However, some of Grievous's [[IG-100 MagnaGuard]]s destroyed the [[shuttle]], along with the two [[Cloning|clones]], before they could make the communication. Fisto was ultimately the only member of the group to survive the mission to Vassek 3. ===Decline under the Empire=== ====A bad reputation==== {{Quote|Rearguard actions across the board…the Twenty-First was on Bestine.|Maximian Ajax, to Hazram Namir|audio=Twenty-First.flac|''[[Battlefront: Twilight Company]]''}} The Clone Wars [[Mission to Mustafar|ended]] in [[19 BBY]] with the fall of the Separatists and the Republic's [[Proclamation of the New Order|transition]] into the [[Galactic Empire]]. The Empire conducted a brutal annexation of Bestine IV''[[Star Wars: Geektionary: The Galaxy from A - Z]]'' and established a [[Imperial naval base|military base]] on the island of [[Jahnae]] in order to quell further rebel incursions in the Inner Rim following the Separatist activity there during the war.''[[Entertainment Weekly's Ultimate Guide to Rogue One]]'' Publicly a major [[Navy|naval]] [[shipyard]], the military installation was rumored to also serve as a research and development facility that produced weapons of war. [[File:BestineNavalBase-BountyHunters29.jpg|thumb|right|300px|The Imperial base on Bestine IV drove away many locals.]] The locals disliked the Empire's presence,[[Bounty Hunters 28|''Bounty Hunters'' 28]] and many denizens were ultimately driven off Bestine IV. One such native was the independent merchant [[Jek Tono Porkins|Jek Porkins]], whose long-lasting disgust with the Empire's authoritarianism had reached a breaking point after witnessing the government's abuses during the construction of the base.{{EncyclopediaCite|Pilots of the Rebel Alliance}} After leaving his [[homeworld]], Porkins joined the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic|Rebel Alliance]] against the Empire as a [[Rebel pilot|pilot]]. One [[Unidentified village (Bestine IV)|village]] remained on Jahnae as a place of residence for the staff at the military base. An [[Bestine IV insurgents|insurgent]] group also stayed to [[Insurrection on Bestine IV|fight]] the Empire, reportedly hiding in the village. Consequently, the Empire struggled to keep the peace on Bestine IV. In [[3 ABY]],{{BTCdate}} during the [[Galactic Civil War]] between the Alliance and the Empire, the Alliance's [[Twenty-First]] was [[Mission to Bestine IV (Twenty-First)|present]] on Bestine IV as a part of a coordinated effort to distract [[Imperial Military|forces]] and allow the [[Rebel Alliance Navy|Alliance fleet]] to complete its [[Mid Rim Retreat|withdrawal]] from the [[Mid Rim Territories]]. News of the operations reached the Alliance's [[61st Mobile Infantry]], where [[Sergeant]] [[Maximian Ajax]] updated [[First Sergeant]] [[Hazram Namir]] about the actions of the Twenty-First and other rebel units. ====Corruption in Bsellis City==== {{RPGseed}} Elsewhere on Bestine IV, the [[Bestine Security Force]] operated in [[Bsellis City]]. However, the [[spice]] gang known as the [[Nova Razors]], the most ruthless of Bestine's criminal gangs, operated out of a tenement building in the [[city]]'s [[Bsellis City market district|market district]] named [[Blue Garden Homes]] and [[Slavery|enslaved]] locals and forced them to refine their spice. Nova Razors' [[Unidentified Twi'lek gang leader|leader]] had a protection deal with the corrupt security Sergeant [[Mey Kilrow]] that allowed the gang to operate without interference by the security force. At one point, a warrior passed through the neighborhood, learning about its troubles with the spice gang and the Bestine Security Force corruption. The warrior was also approached by a [[Youngling|child]] named [[Hawk (boy)|Hawk]], a resident of Blue Garden Homes who offered them low-grade spice. In the middle of their conversation, Kilrow arrived, dismissing the [[Gender|boy]], and introduced herself to the warrior, explaining where Hawk was from and that gang activity there was too dangerous for the Bestine Security to patrol. The warrior spotted Hawk selling spice again within [[Standard hour|hours]], with the child leading them to Blue Garden Homes and identifying the Nova Razors' headquarters. They [[Attack on the Nova Razors|fought]] their way into Blue Garden Homes, defeating gang members and freeing those enslaved by them. Working up the floors, the warrior found the gang leader and his [[Lieutenant (criminal)|lieutenants]]. They defeated the leader, who revealed his protection deal with Kilrow, and subsequently, the warrior attempted to make sure the corrupt [[security officer]] did not set up a similar situation again. {{Endgame}} ===Crimson Dawn strikes=== ====Dual preparation==== {{Quote|''We'' know Crimson Dawn's operatives will be targeting an ''Imperial transport ship''…but what they don't know—what they can't know—is we will be waiting.|Beilert Valance briefs the Revengers|}} [[File:EdgehawkOnBestine-BountyHunters29.png|thumb|left|300px|T'onga's crew was hired to help the Bestine IV insurgents.]] Between 3 [['ABY-BBY' dating system|ABY]] and [[4 ABY]],The events of [[Bounty Hunters 28|''Bounty Hunters'' 28]] take place after the [[Escape from Cloud City]] and before the [[Rescue of Han Solo]], which ''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]'' dates to [[3 ABY]] and [[4 ABY]], respectively. a shipment of munitions traveled to Bestine IV's military base in order for it to finally put a stop to the local insurgent activities. Having learned of the shipment and the unrest on the planet, the criminal syndicate [[Crimson Dawn]] hired a [[T'onga's crew|crew]] of [[bounty hunter]]s led by [[T'onga]] to intercept the [[Unidentified Imperial transport|transport]] in hopes that it would spark chaos in the relations between the Empire and the world's populace. The Empire, however, had simultaneously also learned of Crimson Dawn's plans to attack the [[transport]]. The [[Dark Lord of the Sith|Sith Lord]] [[Anakin Skywalker|Darth Vader]] sent the [[cyborg]] [[mercenary]] [[Beilert Valance]] with the [[Revengers]], a trio of fighters seeking revenge on Crimson Dawn,[[Darth Vader (2020) 18|''Darth Vader'' (2020) 18]] to stop the attack as a test of their loyalty. Valance was being blackmailed by Vader, who knew the location of [[Yuralla Vega]] and [[Cadeliah]], two people the mercenary wanted to keep safe.[[Bounty Hunters 18|''Bounty Hunters'' 18]] The [[Vader's crew|group]] of four were told that the transport was taking medicine and supplies to the village, convincing them that they were helping the locals. ====Clash and revelations==== {{Quote|What happened to you? After all those Imps have done… I mean, transporting weapons to wipe out the village by the military base… that's not like you. Last time I saw you, it seemed like you were trying to escape from their clutches.''"
"''You think I wanted ''this?'' Vader knows where I hid ''Cadeliah—''the girl Nakano Lash was protecting. I stashed her with ''Yura'' on a ''rebel'' base. I have to do ''this…'' to keep them ''safe!''|T'onga and Beilert Valance|[[Bounty Hunters 30|''Bounty Hunters'' 30]]}} [[File:InterceptionOnBestine-BountyHunters29.jpg|thumb|right|300px|T'onga's crew intercepts the Imperial transport on Bestine IV.]] T'onga and Valance briefed their separate crews and arrived on Bestine IV. While T'onga and her cohorts met with the local insurgents, Valance and the Revengers arrived aboard the Imperial transport and prepared to defend it. T'onga's strike team made their run on the transport using the insurgents' [[speeder bike]]s and eliminated a number of Imperial [[Coastal defender stormtrooper|shoretrooper]] sentries before the Revengers engaged the [[bounty]] [[Hunting|hunters]] in combat. The shoretrooper force also sprung a trap on the insurgents, leading to a firefight. The [[Unidentified Bestine IV insurgent|insurgent leader]] attempted to reach the transport's [[Bridge (starship)|bridge]] with T'onga, only to be shot down by Valance. The mercenary, though, recognized T'onga as an ally from the past. Valance and T'onga spoke, surprised at each other's allegiances. After Valance explained his situation with Vader, T'onga revealed that Crimson Dawn had taken Cadeliah while Vega had been killed in an Imperial [[Battle of Panisia|attack]], leading Valance to break down over his failure to protect them. Meanwhile, the Revengers and the Imperial security forces captured the rest of T'onga's bounty hunter crew and awaited further orders from Valance. Valance, though, had changed his mind about working with them, and when he returned to the security, he began massacring them in a fit of rage. He further revealed to the Revengers that the transport was shipping explosives instead of medicine. ====Base or bait==== {{Quote|The attack was a success! But we'd better get out of here before the Imps send reinforcements.''"
"''That was just a means to an end.''"
"''We protected the village. What other possible end is there?''"
"''Bait.|T'onga and Beilert Valance|}} Two [[TIE/ln space superiority starfighter|TIE fighters]] arrived to intervene, but Valance used a [[thermal detonator]] to destroy one of them. The other was destroyed by the [[Edgehawk (starship)|''Edgehawk'']], the starship of T'onga's crew that was [[pilot]]ed by the [[droid]] bounty hunter [[4-LOM]]. Meanwhile, Vader and Valance's [[commanding officer]], Lieutenant [[Jyala Haydenn]], were aboard the [[Imperial-class Star Destroyer|''Imperial''-class Star Destroyer]] ''[[Righteous Fist]]'' in Bestine IV's orbit. Valance contacted Haydenn, with whom he was engaged in a romantic relationship, confronting her about her lying to him about Vega being alive. Afterward, the mercenary let the Imperial munitions transport accelerate toward Bestine's military base, with himself, the Revengers, and the bounty hunters all escaping to the village.[[Bounty Hunters 31|''Bounty Hunters'' 31]] [[File:VillageVictory-BountyHunters30.png|thumb|left|300px|Villagers celebrate the destruction of the Imperial naval base.]] The base reported the transport's acceleration shortly before it crashed into the facility, destroying it in a fireball that was cheered on by the village's residents. Valance, however, had additionally intended for the explosion to serve as bait for Vader. The [[Sith Lord]] indeed then arrived on a [[Lambda-class T-4a shuttle|''Lambda''-class T-4a shuttle]] with Haydenn by his side. Valance confronted and fought Vader, with the pair's skirmish being seen from the village, where the Revengers had taken refuge. Having sent her crew back to the ''Edgehawk'', T'onga attempted to intervene with a [[speeder]] bike but was swiftly stopped by Vader, and one of her crew had to rescue her when Haydenn attempted to pursue. ====Punishment==== {{Quote|Even if you kill me, at least I know we saved the people in that village.''"
"''You did not save those guerilla sympathizers—you doomed them.|Beilert Valance and Darth Vader|}} [[File:VillageBombed-BountyHunters31.jpg|thumb|right|250px|TIE bombers destroy the village.]] The fight ended with Vader [[Telekinesis|throwing]] Valance to the ground with [[the Force]]. At that time, [[TIE/sa tactical bomber|TIE/sa bombers]] arrived and bombed the village, with the Revengers having to flee into a cave. The Sith Lord moved in to kill Valance, but Haydenn stepped in to do it herself. Despite Valance's pleas for them to flee together, she shot the mercenary in the head, sending him falling off the cliff and into the [[Fire|burning]] village. Displeased that Valance's body had gone beyond their reach, Vader had Haydenn send a recovery unit to search for the mercenary's body. Valance, however, had survived the shot and the fall and fled on the ''Edgehawk'' after T'onga's crew found him first. With the recovery team failing to recover Valance, Vader spoke with Haydenn again aboard the ''Righteous Fist'' above Bestine IV, advising her to send the Empire's best trackers to find the mercenary. At Vader's request, she summoned the [[Imperial Special Forces|special forces]] unit [[Inferno Squad]] and briefed them on a [[Hunt for Valance|mission]] to find Valance and [[Memory wipe|wipe]] his memory to remove any classified Imperial [[DS-2 Death Star II Mobile Battle Station|secrets]] he might have witnessed. In [[34 ABY]],''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]'' dates the events of [[Star Wars: Galactic Starcruiser|''Star Wars'': Galactic Starcruiser]] to [[34 ABY]]. a partial [[Star map|map]] of [[the galaxy]] that indicated Bestine's position was displayed on several [[Viewscreen|screens]] aboard [[Chandrila Star Line]]'s [[MPO-1400 Purgill-class star cruiser|Star Cruiser]] ''[[Halcyon]]''.[[Star Wars: Galactic Starcruiser|''Star Wars'': Galactic Starcruiser]] ==Inhabitants== {{Quote|The job? It's simple. Help us cause a little trouble for the Empire—specifically on a planet with an Imperial outpost barely keeping the peace over a local populace that doesn't want them there.|Crimson Dawn operative [[Margo]], to T'onga|}} Bestine IV was home to humans like Jek Porkins, as well as a [[Dowutin]], [[Twi'lek]], and the [[Shahkirin]] [[Technician|mechanic]] [[Yipsit]], who grew up on Bestine's cliffs before joining the [[Resistance]]. The Bestine Security Force operated in Bsellis City during the time of the Empire, with one of their [[officer]]s being the corrupt Sergeant Mey Kilrow. Bestine IV's Imperial base maintained a complement of security forces, including shoretroopers. ==Locations== {{Quote|We're receiving another signal. This one from the base at ''Jahnae''.|An [[Imperial officer]], to Jyala Haydenn, aboard the ''Righteous Fist''|}} Bestine IV's islands included Jahnae, where an Imperial naval shipyard was located, accompanied by a village for its staff in a nearby valley. Among the world's settlements was Bsellis City, which had a market district where the housing tenement Blue Garden Homes was located. ==Behind the scenes== ===Origins=== {{Quote|My friend has a friend on Bestine who might help us make contact.|Biggs Darklighter, to Luke Skywalker, in a deleted scene for ''Star Wars:'' Episode IV ''A New Hope''|{{Film|IV}} {{Del}}}} [[File:Bestine_eaw.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Bestine IV, as depicted in the ''Star Wars'' Legends continuity]] Bestine IV, first known as simply Bestine, originated in "Tosche Station," a deleted scene of [[George Lucas]]' [[1977]] [[original trilogy]] film, [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars:'' Episode IV ''A New Hope'']]. The [[1976|prior year]], the line mentioning [[Bestine IV/Legends|Bestine]] was adapted in the film's [[Star Wars: A New Hope (novelization)|novelization]], written by [[Alan Dean Foster]].[[Star Wars: A New Hope (novelization)|''Star Wars Episode IV: A New Hope'' novelization]] Bestine IV's full name was first given in ''[[Galaxy Guide 1: A New Hope]]'', a [[Star Wars Legends|''Star Wars'' Legends]] supplement to [[West End Games]]' ''[[Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game]]'' released in [[1989]].''[[Galaxy Guide 1: A New Hope]]'' The world's first appearance in that continuity was in the [[1993]] [[LucasArts]] [[Star Wars video games|video game]] [[Star Wars: X-Wing (video game)|''Star Wars: X-Wing'']].[[Star Wars: X-Wing (video game)|''Star Wars: X-Wing'']] ===Canon developments=== In the current ''[[Star Wars]]'' [[canon]], Bestine was first mentioned in "[[Lair of Grievous]]," the tenth episode of the [[The Clone Wars: Season One|first season]] of the animated television show ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]'', which first aired on [[December 12]], [[2008]].{{SWArchive|url=theclonewars/guide/episode010.html|text=''The Clone Wars'' Episode Guide: Lair of Grievous}} Its full name, Bestine IV, was introduced into canon through Jek Porkin's card for Base Series 1 of the [[Topps]] mobile game [[Star Wars: Card Trader|''Star Wars:'' Card Trader]],{{SWCT|set=Base Series 1|cardname=Jek Porkins - X-Wing Pilot}} released on [[March 11]], [[2015]].{{ToppsDigital|url=swcardtrader/article/545bbb5771100031fdcbef4e|text=Base Series 1 is here!|date=2015-03-11}} ''[[Knights of Fate]]'', a [[2018]]{{FantasyFlightGames|url=en/news/2018/6/21/way-of-the-warrior|text=Way of the Warrior}} [[Fantasy Flight Games]] sourcebook published as part of the ''[[Star Wars: Force and Destiny]]'' [[Star Wars Roleplaying|roleplaying game]] system, includes an adventure idea that is set on Bestine IV and designed for a group of player characters including a representative of the Warrior class. The suggested scenario culminates with a multi-choice objective to confront Mey Kilrow and stop her from continuing to make corrupt deals. The suggested choices of approaching the confrontation include intimidating her, setting her up for apprehension by local authorities, or fighting her. She will immediately call for backup if attacked, forcing the player characters to flee—including from the attention of the Imperials if they openly use [[Force power]]s. Kilrow herself prefers to flee over fighting to the death. This article assumes the adventure scenario plays out as described. In the [[2019]] video game ''[[Star Wars Jedi: Fallen Order]]'', a light-blue-and-white cosmetic skin named "Bestine" can be unlocked for use by the in-game droid companion, [[BD-1]]. Located in the [[Ice Caves]] of the planet [[Zeffo]], the collectible is guarded by a [[Purge Trooper]] and a [[Stormtrooper Commander|scout trooper commander]].''[[Star Wars Jedi: Fallen Order]]'' Bestine IV's first appearance in canon was in the [[Bounty Hunters 28|twenty-eighth issue]] of [[Marvel Comics]]' ''[[Star Wars: Bounty Hunters]]'' series of [[Star Wars comic books|comic books]]. The issue was written by [[Ethan Sacks]], illustrated by [[Paolo Villanelli]], and published on [[November 2]], [[2022]].{{Marvel|url=comics/issue/103048/star_wars_bounty_hunters_2020_28|text=Star Wars: Bounty Hunters (2020) #28}} ===Inconsistencies=== The [[Star Wars: Build Your Own X-Wing 22|twentieth issue]] of [[De Agostini]]'s ''[[Star Wars: Build Your Own X-Wing]]'' magazine series, which was released in [[January]] 2019,{{WebCite|url=https://www.model-space.com/us/build-star-wars-x-wing-model.html|text=Star Wars Build your own X-wing | 1:18 Model on De Agostini Model Space|archivedate=20180819033322}} indicates that issues of ''[[Star Wars: Build Your Own X-Wing]]'' were shipped in sets of four every month starting with [[August]] [[2018]]. Thus, it can be deduced that issue 22 was released in [[January]] [[2019]]. establishes that Bestine IV was located near Kestic Station. However, "[[Pilots of the Rebel Alliance]]," an issue of De Agostini's [[Star Wars Encyclopedia (series)|''Star Wars Encyclopedia'']] magazine series released on [[March 4]], 2022,{{Altaya|lang=fr|url=livres-bd/encyclopedie-star-wars|text=Official Star Wars Encyclopedia}} states that Kestic Station was instead a location on Bestine itself.
